cohort: 314 singleton births to women with joint hypermobility syndrome/Ehlers-Danlos syndrome before delivery, compared to 1,247,864 singleton births to women without a diagnosis of joint hypermobility syndrome/Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in Sweden from 1997 through 2011
finding: Maternal joint hypermobility syndrome/Ehlers-Danlos syndrome was not associated with an increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preterm birth, preterm premature rupture of membranes, cesarean section, stillbirth, low Apgar score, small for gestational age, or large for gestational age.
mod_finding: Women with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome had a higher risk of induction of labor and amniotomy, but no excess risks for adverse pregnancy outcome were seen in joint hypermobility syndrome.
